title: ABA/123/2024 of SUKHDEV SINGH Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Anticipatory Bail Application No. 123 of 2024
Sukhdev Singh ...Applicant
Versus

State of Uttarakhand ...Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Deep Prakash Bhatt, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Akshay Latwal, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicant seeks anticipatory bail in FIR No. 326 of
2022, under Section 376 IPC, Police Station Nanakmatta,
District Udham Singh Nagar.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.
3. According to the FIR, the applicant and the
informant came close to each other in the year 2016. Once the
applicant took the informant in a hotel; there he established
physical relations with the informant and assured to marry
her. They continued their relationship for a long. According to
the FIR, subsequently the applicant declined to marry the
victim and also threatened her that if she approaches the
applicant, he would make her photographs and videos viral.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit
that the applicant and the victim both were major. Their

2
relationship was consensual. Nothing was concealed from the
victim.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that the victim
has supported the prosecution case during investigation.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant would also
submit that the charge sheet has been filed in the case.
Summons could not be served on the applicant because he is
in the Indian Army. Straightway non bailable warrants have
been issued.
7. The order sheets have been placed for the perusal
of the Court.
8. Learned State counsel admits this fact that
summons could not be served on the applicant.
9. Perusal of the order sheets reveals that though non
bailable warrants were issued against the applicant, but it
does not show that ever bailable warrants or summons were
served on the applicant. The order sheets are taken on record.
10. Having considered the entirety of facts, this Court
is of the view that this is a case fit for anticipatory bail.
11. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.
12. In the eventuality of arrest, the applicant shall be
enlarged on anticipatory bail subject to his furnishing a

3
personal bond with two sureties, each in the like amount, to
the satisfaction of the court concerned. In addition to it, the
applicant shall also comply with the following conditions:
(i) The applicant shall not approach any witness in
any manner, whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall not leave the country without
prior permission of the concerned court.
(iii) The applicant shall deposit his passport with the
court concerned. The passport may only be
returned by the order of the court concerned. In
case the applicant does not have passport, he shall
give an undertaking to that effect to the court
concerned.
(v) The applicant shall also give an undertaking on (i)
& (ii) above.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 14.05.2024
Jitendra
